newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - November 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - November 18.

text.p: Following are the highlights of stories reported in the Irish press on Monday.
- Northern Ireland's main unionist parties have responded to renewed speculation about an IRA ceasefire, significantly toughening their demands on decommissioning of paramilitary weapons.
- Significant changes in the work of police have been suggested by management consultants examining the force on behalf of a Government-appointed review group.

- Changes in the constitution to prohibit discrimination and guarantee all citizens a right to education are expected to be recommended by the Commission on the Status of People with disabilities in its final report today.
- Ireland's Attorney General Dermot Gleeson has come under renewed assault from the country's main opposition party for his role in the controversy over judicial misconduct.
- The minister for finance, Ruairi Quinn has revised his estimates for the current budget surplus upwards to between 200 million to 250 million Irish Pounds for 1997.
- Up to 90,000 pig carcases with antibiotic residues are likely to have passed into the human food chain last year.

- The Northern Ireland peace process is facing a critical phase as Sinn Fein awaits a response from the British government to ""soundings'' on how soon after an IRA ceasefire it might be allowed into the multi-party talks.
- The government is fearful that Justice minister Nora Owen's position will come under severe threat again this week as the inquiry into the judicial fracas is published.

- Unions are demanding a 1.1 billion Irish Pound package in tax cuts in the pay talks this week and a confidential Department of Finance report is predicting the creation of 33,000 jobs a year until 1999.
